findings.title: Silence menu item is shown in the list view but clicking it does nothing
findings.body: In the new list view, RuleActionsButtons is called with only promRule (rule/rulerRule is undefined). AlertRuleMenu can compute canSilence=true from the new prom-based abilities (useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities returns a Silence ability for Grafana alerting rules), so the 'Silence notifications' menu item is rendered and calls handleSilence, which sets showSilenceDrawer=true. However, the drawer is only rendered behind `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} .../>}`, and rule is undefined in the list view, so no drawer ever appears. The user clicks Silence and nothing happens — a broken, dead menu action. Either the silence ability should not be granted without a ruler rule, or the drawer needs to work from the prom rule/identifier.

findings.title: Delete menu item can never appear in the alert list view
findings.body: The Delete menu item is guarded by `{canDelete && rulerRule && ...}`. In the list view (GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons), only promRule is passed and rulerRule is undefined, so Delete is never rendered even when canDelete is true via the new prom-based abilities. This is a regression: users could previously delete Grafana rules from the list view. The guard appears unnecessary because RuleActionsButtons' handleDelete ignores the rulerRule argument entirely (`handleDelete={() => showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)}`) and the delete modal works off the rule identifier, which is now derived from the prom rule. The updated GrafanaGroupLoader test codifies the regression by asserting the menu has exactly 4 items with no Delete.

findings.title: Pause/unpause no longer available from the list view despite canPause being computed
findings.body: The pause menu item requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, but in the list view rulerRule is always undefined now (ruler API was removed), so MenuItemPauseRule can never render there even when canPause is true via the new useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities path. The grafana-based pause ability is computed and OR'd in but can never result in a visible action, making that check dead code and silently dropping the pause/unpause feature from the list view. If dropping pause is intentional, the prom-based Pause ability should not be requested here; if not, MenuItemPauseRule needs a prom-rule-based variant.

findings.title: Duplicate action can be wrongly enabled for cloud rules based on Grafana-rule permissions
findings.body: For non-Grafana (cloud) rules, promRule is not a Grafana prom rule, so useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is called with skipToken, i.e. useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined). With rule=undefined, duplicateSupported evaluates to true (not provisioned, not plugin-provided, not loading) and the 'allowed' side is getRulesPermissions('grafana').create — i.e. the Grafana-managed rule create permission. Because canDuplicate ORs the ruler-based and grafana-based abilities, a user who has the Grafana rule-create permission but lacks alert.rules.external.write will now see an enabled 'Duplicate' menu item on Mimir/Cortex/Prometheus rules, whereas before this PR the ability was purely ruler-based and correctly gated on the external write permission. The backend will still reject the save, but the UI now offers an action the user is not permitted to perform.

findings.title: Federated rule group check lost for CombinedRule-based abilities
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities was refactored to delegate to useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2). The old implementation computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and treated federated (Mimir cross-tenant) rule groups as immutable, blocking Update/Delete. useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes `const isFederated = false` with a TODO. Since the still-widely-used useAlertRuleAbility hook goes through useAllAlertRuleAbilities, federated rule groups are now considered editable/removable in all consumers of that hook (e.g. the v1 list view RuleActionsButtons), letting users attempt edits/deletes on federated rules that the ruler API will reject.

findings.title: Prom-based abilities wrongly restrict Export/Pause/Restore to alerting rules, excluding Grafana recording rules
findings.body: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, ModifyExport, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently are gated on `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. The ruler-based equivalent (useAllRulerRuleAbilities) gates these on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is true for both Grafana alerting AND recording rules. Grafana recording rules can be paused and can be exported via modify-export, so in the list view (which now only has the prom rule) recording rules lose the Export and Pause actions that they previously had. Use a check that covers both Grafana prom rule types instead of alertingRule.

findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a React key in filtered results
findings.body: In the rules.map switch, the 'grafana' branch returns <GrafanaRuleListItem .../> without key={key}, while the 'datasource' and default branches both pass key={key} (and the previous code passed key to GrafanaRuleLoader). Mixing keyed and unkeyed siblings in the same list triggers React's missing-key warning and makes reconciliation fall back to index-based identity for those items, which can cause state mixups as pages of results are appended.

findings.title: Rule view link lost the returnTo parameter
findings.body: The old GrafanaRuleListItem built the href as createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }) using createReturnTo(), so navigating back from the rule detail view returned the user to the rule list. The new component builds the href without returnTo, so the 'back' navigation from a rule opened from the list (grouped view or filter view) no longer returns to the list — a small but concrete UX regression.

findings.title: Stale comment and variable name reference removed ruler preloading
findings.body: The ruler prefetch dispatch was removed from getGroupsAndProvideCache, but the comment above the block still says 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX. Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded', and the variable is still named cacheAndRulerPreload. The comment now describes behavior that no longer exists and is misleading to future readers.
